_comment: Example Android configuration with llama-server ablation support
_description: This configuration demonstrates how to enable llama-server for accurate Android ablation studies
_comment_storage: Use shared storage for easy access from file manager
_comment_tests: Enable ablation studies with llama-server support
_comment_android_config: AndroidConfig settings for llama-server ablation support

android_config._description: Configuration for Android llama-server ablation support
android_config._comment_ablation: Enable ablation studies mode for automatic llama-server selection
android_config._comment_backend: Explicit backend selection (null = auto-detect based on ablation + platform)

_comment_ablation_scenarios: Ablation scenarios will use these cache configurations:

cold_cache.description: Cache enabled but empty (first request creates cache)

warm_cache.description: Cache enabled and populated (subsequent requests reuse cache)

_comment_thermal: Longer sleep time to prevent overheating on mobile
_comment_output: Lightweight output formats for mobile storage
_comment_setup_instructions: - AndroidBackend will detect enable_ablation_studies=true on Android platform
- System will automatically use llama-server if binary is available
- Control runs will have true no-cache baseline (--cache-ram 0 --no-cache-prompt)
- Cache scenarios will have proper per-request cache control
- Fallback to llama-cli with warning if llama-server not available
_comment_troubleshooting: - Rebuild if needed: cd ~/llama.cpp && cmake --build build --config Release
- Set custom path in android_config.llama_server_path if needed
If ablation studies show no difference:
- Verify control runs show cache_mode=none in logs
- Monitor llama-server logs for cache activity
- Reduce context_size and max_tokens for memory constraints
- Use Q2_K quantization for limited RAM devices
